findings.source_quote: πλὴν πρώτη μοιχεία ἐστὶν τὸ ἄνδρα μὴ ἰδίᾳ μόνῃ χρήσασθαι γυναικὶ καὶ γυναῖκα μὴ ἰδίῳ μόνῳ χρήσασθαι ἀνδρί.
findings.english_quote: But the first is adultery: a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband.
findings.issue: The draft chooses an elliptical reading in which adultery is the first previously mentioned kind of sexual immorality. That is possible, but πρώτη is feminine and can qualify μοιχεία itself; it does not directly agree with the preceding neuter εἴδη. The alternative understanding, ‘the first/primary adultery consists in ...,’ is not disclosed. The lexical note presents the enumeration reading without acknowledging this syntactic uncertainty.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a meaning-level source_issues note distinguishing the draft’s elliptical enumeration reading from the alternative ‘the first/primary form of adultery consists in ...’. Compare the adjective–noun–articular-infinitive construction with comparable usage before settling the main wording. Preserve the supplied Greek; this is not evidence of a transcription defect. Any replacement wording requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: work for a craftsperson, mercy for one who is inactive.
findings.issue: Bare ‘inactive’ foregrounds nonparticipation rather than weakness or incapacity. In the contrast with providing work to a craftsperson, ἀδρανεῖ can designate someone lacking the strength or ability to work. The existing note acknowledges inability to work, but the main wording does not adequately convey that contextually important possibility.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the provisional replacement ‘work for a craftsperson, mercy for someone unable to work’ with the current wording. Retain a note explaining that ἀδρανής can mean weak or incapable as well as inactive; do not present incapacity as lexically certain. Review the revised wording afresh before acceptance.

findings.source_quote: τοῦ νῦν μόνου μακροθύμου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ
findings.english_quote: who alone is now patient and good
findings.issue: The main rendering is grammatically defensible and preserves the supplied μόνου. However, the lexical note treats its agreement with God as conclusively determining the focus of exclusivity. Agreement supports the person-exclusive reading, but the contrast between present patience and the ensuing judgment also raises a possible present-mode interpretation, ‘who is now only patient and good.’ That less straightforward interpretation is neither evaluated nor preserved as uncertainty. It must also be distinguished from ‘only for now,’ which can suggest that the attributes themselves will cease.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the supplied μόνου and qualify the lexical rationale. Add a meaning-level source_issues note identifying ‘who alone is now patient and good’ as the straightforward person-exclusive reading and explaining the contextual pressure toward a present-mode reading without certifying that alternative. Seek comparable usage in this author or period before excluding it categorically. Do not silently substitute μόνον or change the main text merely to harmonize the theology. Any revised wording or note requires fresh review.
